conventions.axes: Unity axes, metres. Unity x = -Blender x, Unity y = Blender z (up), Unity z = -Blender y. Assumes the kit FBX files are imported with Bake Axis Conversion so each kit object's local axes are Unity axes.
conventions.groups: Pieces that share kit object and material are grouped. Each instance is [object, position, rotation_euler_deg, scale, placement], the KEY POSE (before any motion channel). group.motion lists the same objects in the same order.
conventions.instance.rotation_euler_deg: Unity Euler angles in degrees (Quaternion.Euler(x, y, z)), rounded to 1 degree.
conventions.instance.position: Metres, rounded to 1 mm: the piece's pivot (its base centre, the kit convention; the sword, dagger, funnel and whirl bands, rays and soft rays pivot at their origin: the guard, or the axis foot).
conventions.instance.scale: A number for uniform scale, else [x, y, z] in Unity local axes.
conventions.group.kit_object: The object inside group.kit. A kit of enemy_model means a second skin of the enemy model itself (stone, black) shown over it in the given window; unity_shader_mockup means a shell to build as a shader on the real model.
conventions.group.material: The material the piece wears in the render (shared meshes are re-coloured per piece). Flat emission bands, as pass 2.
conventions.timing: animated. Every piece is keyed at 20 fps; time 0 is frame 7 (frames 1-6 are a 0.3 s lead-in), and each timeline ends with 0.5 s of settle.
conventions.motion: One entry per instance (same order): verb, visible [appear, vanish] s (a vanish of 9 or more means it stays), delay = appear time, duration, easing, and the channels: path = [[t, offset (Unity axes, world-aligned), easing into this key]], scale_keys = [[t, multiplier on the key-pose scale (Unity local x, y, z), easing]], spin = {axis (Unity), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied as Quaternion.AngleAxis(degrees, axis) * keyRotation about the pivot, orbit = {centre (Unity, from the origin), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied last about the vertical through the centre, follow_body = the body index whose motion the piece rides on. Before the first key a channel holds its first value, after the last its last. Easings: linear, out = 1-(1-x)^2, in = x^2, inout = smoothstep, outback = overshoot (c = 1.70158), step = jump at the key. Angles are in Unity's sense.
conventions.bodies: The enemy model (enemy_husk stand-in) per body with its own motion (path, scale_keys, spin, spin2 applied after spin); body 0 is the one the reaction lands on. The stand-ins face the player.
conventions.lights: None: every look is unlit beyond the scene sun.
conventions.ribbons: Curve ribbons (wind curls, lightning arcs, floor combs, chains of light) are not kit meshes: each lists its points (Unity axes, metres, relative to its centre), width_m, radius_profile (taper = thin tail to full head scaled by taper_tail_head; needle = thin at both ends; flat = even), material and ink. Build them as a tube or flat ribbon along the points with the ink outline.

verbs.ribbon_draw: draw_on = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is drawn from tail to head (the head leads). erase = [[t, fraction, easing]]: how much is wiped from the tail toward the head. Visible length = draw_on - erase; nothing pops in or out.
verbs.orbit: centre (player, station or body n), radius (m), turns_per_second (Unity sense, + = counter-clockwise from above), start (s), rise (m per s), and optional angle_keys added on top. The ribbon turns about the vertical axis through its centre from start.
verbs.spiral: an orbit with rise > 0: the ribbon climbs while it turns.

conventions.scale: Stand-in enemies are 1.89 m tall, the size of the castle soldiers. Pieces were drawn to read at the game camera (12.7 m); keep their size relative to the body in game, not to the screen.
conventions.source: staging/blender/2026-11-21_strikes/strikes.blend, scene ST, one station per thrust look (x from 58000, 40 m apart, in the order earth, ice, fire, water, lightning, metal, life, dark, poison, light, wind). Built by script (thrust/tools/thrust_specs.py) from the elements 2, 3 and 4 kits, combo kit v3 and the arc strikes kit vfx_strikes_kit.fbx. No new meshes: there is no thrust kit file.
conventions.made: 2026-11-21 by Claude through the Blender MCP connection.
conventions.strike_shape: thrust: the Great Spear's infused strike, attack_spear_1 (Weapons.cs:206): a straight thrust after a 0.14 s windup, active 0.07 s, Reach 4.0 m, along a lane 0.9 m wide (closer than 1.4 m only the haft hits). The effect drives out along the lane from the spear tip, hits the enemies in the lane, then settles.
conventions.origin: Every position is relative to the PLAYER's ground point (y = 0), where the thrust starts. The lane runs along lane_direction (Unity axes; the renders turn the player and lane 35 degrees toward the camera's right so the lane reads across the screen). Pieces with about_player (placement c) and ribbons whose centre is player are drawn about the player; bodies carry their positions from it; ribbons whose centre is "body k" are relative to that body's ground point. In game, turn the whole look so lane_direction is the player's facing at the thrust.
conventions.front_timing: The front leaves the spear tip at 1.8 m at t 0 (the end of the windup) and drives out to 4.6 m by 0.13 s, easing out, so it is at the tip's full reach (4.0 m) as the tip gets there at 0.07 s. Everything on the lane is timed to the front passing it; front_reaches_s gives the time it reaches each struck body. In Unity key them off the thrust's own tip, not a fixed delay.
conventions.instance.placement: g = on the ground, b = on or around a body, c = about the player (along the lane).
conventions.carrier: The grey stand-in spear in the renders (stk_spear, role ref, a 3.5 m spear at chest height) is a mock-up of the thrust only: it is not in this recipe and nothing is drawn on the weapon.
conventions.motion.body: The body (index into bodies) a piece belongs to, with about_body = its position from that body (Unity axes). Written from the pass's specs (thrust/tools/thrust_specs.py) by thrust/tools/thrust_assemble_recipe.py.
conventions.per_struck_enemy: motion.per_struck_enemy = true marks a piece that exists once for each enemy the thrust actually hits, placed about_body from that enemy and timed from the moment the front reaches it; spawn one set per struck enemy and none on a miss. Bodies 0 to 2 are in the lane (struck_bodies); body 3 stands beside it (missed_bodies) and has nothing drawn on it.
conventions.look_fields: Each look carries element, moment (infused), strike_shape (thrust), weapon, lane_direction, owner, answer, look (in words), struck_bodies, missed_bodies, front_reaches_s and per_struck_enemy_pieces.
conventions.dark_outline: Dark's hands (vfxst_hand_big_open, vfxst_hand_big_grip: one rounded organic mesh each; material st_hand_small, near-black with a violet rim) were rendered with a violet outline on their outer silhouette (Freestyle line set InkHands, colour 0.42, 0.18, 0.7 linear, thickness 1.5). Each hand is one merged mesh, so the outline never traces joins between parts. In Unity give them an outline pass in that colour on the silhouette only. The thrust's shadow wisps (vfxe2_cloud_a/_b in st_sl_shadow_smoke) take the same violet silhouette outline.
conventions.poison_veins: Poison's bruise, wound, vein web and sheen are ribbons whose points were snapped onto the stand-in body's surface and sunk into it so they lie flat on the skin (the bruise shows as a flat patch about 1.5 cm proud, the fine vessels as painted lines) and ride its motion (follow_body). In Unity build them as a decal or a vein and bruise mask in the enemy's shader that spreads from the wound with the same timing; nothing should stand out of the body.
conventions.colour: Materials are flat emission in linear colour (ramp ones shade by facing, centre to rim), except the toon stone, which is lit toon with the ink outline. Metal uses the blue-grey st_sl_glint and Poison the sickly-rimmed st_sl_venom, as in the slam and spin. No stop reaches pure white: the strip maker counts pure-white pixels in every strip frame (thrust/white_check.json): every look is 0.
conventions.revisions: 2026-11-21. Round 2 (this recipe), the owner: Ice, Fire, Lightning, Life, Wind and Water approved and unchanged (checked identical to round 1). Metal's glint and Light's glare lifted above the soldiers' shoulders (1.85 m) and run on to 5.3 m down the lane; Dark has one big hand per struck enemy, fanned; Poison's drops spray in an arc off the spear tip and land spread out; Earth's stones tear up on the camera side of the lane too. Round 1: thrust/r1/.
